title: Dev log: starting Ahwa: Heart of the Azure Dragon, a xianxia otome VN in Godot, and this time we have an artist
author: DepartmentPlus5191
selftext:
Hi again, it's Hop. Earlier this month Nibble and I released In Your Hands, a horror sound novel we built with a lot of help from AI. In my launch post I said that for our next project, we'd love to bring an artist onto the team. Well, we've started on the next one, and we have one.



\*\*A new team\*\*



This one is being made in-house at Lusty Robots, the publisher behind In Your Hands. Nibble isn't on this project, but the two of us are planning to team up again for the one after. This time there are three of us:



\* A scenario writer

\* An artist

\* Me, handling programming, staging and UI



\*\*The game\*\*



Ahwa: Heart of the Azure Dragon is an otome visual novel set in a xianxia world, a style of Chinese fantasy built around cultivators, sects and immortals. You play as Ahwa, who inherits a dragon pearl from her mother and, with it, becomes the leader of the Azure Dragon clan. There are six love interests, and the total length isn't locked in yet.



The art started with our scenario writer, who drew the first concept sketches herself. Our artist is building the final style on top of her drawings, so the look of the game comes straight from the person who knows the story best.



\*\*What we learned from In Your Hands\*\*



After launch, one piece of feedback we got was that the options menu had way too many settings. Some parts of the game also felt awkward to players. That stuck with me, so this time I want the staging and UI to feel friendlier from the start. I'm putting extra care into how text appears on screen, and into how the gallery and character profiles are presented, since those are the places otome players spend a lot of time.



\*\*How I'm using AI this time\*\*



Like last time, I'm using Claude Code and Codex for the Godot side, and Suno will probably handle the music again. I also tried Muse recently, but it didn't really fit how I work.



The biggest change for me is that the agent can open Godot and work in it directly while I watch. That means I often jump in before it finishes a task: "this transition is too slow," "move that panel," and so on.



\*\*First look\*\*

https://i.redd.it/1jvbutij9tvh1.png

Here's a sample of the lobby screen, just to give you a feel for the mood we're going for.



\*\*A question for you\*\*



For those of you working with agents like this: do you give feedback while the agent is still working, or wait until it's done and then send everything at once? Interrupting mid-task feels faster to me, but I'm not sure if it makes the results worse. I'd love to hear how others handle it.
